issues.body: `unwritten_integer_lexicals` still proves only that every observed lexical occurred somewhere in the generated sequence; it does not prove that every still-live written RDF term remains in each sparq snapshot. `normalize_term` collapses distinct terms such as `"0105"^^xsd:integer` and `"+105"^^xsd:integer`. Thus, at identical subject/predicate/graph coordinates, a faulty sparq result that drops one spelling but retains the other can normalize to the same single quad as Oxigraph, while the retained lexical remains in `written`, so both the normalized comparison and lexical oracle pass. The added `noncanonical_integer_lexicals_survive_as_distinct_sparq_terms` test checks current engine behavior directly, but does not mutation-test this failure mode through the full adjudication path.
issues.fix_hint: Add a live-term oracle that tracks expected lexical term identities with their quad coordinates and update lifetime, or an equivalent per-operation preservation check. Add a non-vacuity test feeding the full adjudication path two same-value spellings at the same coordinates with a simulated sparq snapshot missing one spelling, and assert rejection. The oracle must distinguish legitimate deletion from accidental collapse and recurse through triple terms.
issues.title: Numeric adjudication still permits loss of a distinct written RDF term

verdict.summary: Round 2 remains blocked by the same soundness hole. The new focused tests establish that sparq currently preserves three spellings and that the one-way unwritten-lexical oracle detects canonicalization, but they do not establish that the full differential rejects loss of one still-live written term. Because normalization maps distinct integer lexical forms to one term and the oracle checks only observed lexicals are a subset of all lexicals generated anywhere in the sequence, a faulty sparq snapshot retaining one written spelling while dropping another can still normalize to Oxigraph's single quad and pass. The requested full-adjudication mutation/non-vacuity case is still absent.
